roadmap.lecture_goal: Develop a comprehensive understanding of how to optimize VR experiences and solve the associated pathfinding problems for efficient virtual tours.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the foundational concepts of optimizing VR experiences by controlling exposure duration and analyzing the methods and limitations of such control.
You'll be able to describe the characteristics of semi-interactive VR tours and define the specific optimization problems involved in creating an efficient tour.
You'll be able to formulate and solve the optimal POI travel problem by transforming it into a Traveling Salesman Problem and applying a two-phase algorithm.

segments.subgoal: Explain the approach of optimizing VR experience by controlling exposure duration

key_points.text: The previous model used to enhance presence does not provide solutions for experience optimization.,
Cyber sickness symptoms rise proportionally with the duration of VR exposure.,
A key optimization approach is controlling exposure duration to minimize cyber sickness.,
The lecture will discuss one specific approach to optimizing VR experience for cyber sickness.

key_terms.definition: Optic flow is the visual speed, defined as the rate at which scenes change in the virtual world, which allows the user to gain the perception of movement. This rate is designed to match the user's perceived instantaneous walking speed.

Cyber sickness is a condition correlated with the duration of exposure in a VR environment. The severity of symptoms associated with cyber sickness rises proportionally with the length of the VR session.
Exposure duration is the length of time a user spends in the virtual world. This duration is a key factor that contributes to the onset and severity of cyber sickness.

segments.subgoal: Analyze methods for controlling VR exposure duration and their limitations

key_points.text: The duration of cyber sickness depends on factors such as virtual world size, travel speed, and interaction time.
Higher travel speed reduces the overall duration of exposure in the virtual world.
Teleportation reduces exposure duration by allowing instantaneous movement, but it lacks naturalness.
Arbitrarily changing the terrain shape prevents users from building a mental map, which hampers wayfinding.

key_terms.definition: A virtual environment is a digital space that can range from very small, such as a room, to very large, like a city. It can also be extremely large, such as a specific island.
Teleportation-type movement is a method of navigation where the speed is at its maximum. This results in instantaneous movement occurring between two specific points.

segments.subgoal: Explain the characteristics and purpose of semi-interactive VR tours

key_points.text: A semi-interactive tour is defined as interaction with Points of Interest (POIs) combined with navigation controlled by the system.
In a semi-interactive tour, travel is automatic and system-controlled, but user interactions are limited to specific objects or POIs.
The primary objective of studying semi-interactive system control tools is to reduce the duration of exposure to the virtual world.

key_terms.definition: A semi-interactive tour is a virtual tour where the travel between locations is managed automatically by the system, but users are allowed to interact with specific objects at designated points of interest. This type of tour does not totally disregard user interactions.
Points of interest are specific, chosen locations within the virtual environment where users are permitted to interact with objects. These are the limited areas where user interaction is allowed.
Interaction time is the specific duration of time required for a user to interact with the virtual objects. This time can be ignored in entirely system-controlled VR tools.

A system-controlled VR tool is a virtual reality application where the movement or travel between points is managed automatically by the system. In this scenario, the interaction time can be disregarded.

segments.subgoal: Define the two optimization problems for creating an efficient VR tour

key_points.text: Interaction time at points of interest can be limited based on an a priori estimate of the average user's required time.
One optimization approach seeks an optimum path that allows users to experience all points of interest in minimum time.
The second optimization approach seeks an optimum path that maximizes the number of points of interest within a fixed time limit.
These two approaches provide methods for optimizing the duration of exposure in a virtual tour.

key_terms.definition: Points of interest are specific locations within the virtual environment that users are intended to interact with or explore during a tour. These locations are the focus of the time optimization process.

A semi-interactive tour is a virtual tour design that imposes a limit on the amount of time a user can spend interacting at any single point of interest. This time limit is used to optimize the overall duration of the experience.
Duration of exposure refers to the total time a user spends experiencing a virtual tour. This duration is the primary variable that the optimization process seeks to improve.

Optimum path is the most efficient route designed to meet a specific goal within the virtual tour. This path either ensures all points of interest are visited in minimum time or maximizes the number of points visited within a fixed time.

segments.subgoal: Formulate the optimal POI travel problem using graph theory

key_points.text: The virtual world is modeled as a weighted graph G, where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges.
Vertices (V) represent all the Points of Interest (POIs) in the virtual world.
Edge weights are determined by the Euclidean distance between two connected POIs.
The graph does not need to be complete because direct paths between all POIs are not guaranteed in realistic environments.
The objective is to find a path that covers all vertices while minimizing the time required and maintaining a realistic speed.

key_terms.definition: Weighted graph is a representation of the virtual world where the connections between points of interest are assigned numerical values. These weights typically denote the distance between the connected points.
Vertex is a node in the graph that represents a specific point of interest within the virtual world. Each point of interest is assumed to be a vertex in the graph structure.

Edge weight is the value assigned to an edge between two vertices, representing the Euclidean distance between them if a direct path exists. If the vertices are not directly connected, the edge weight is assigned a very large number, denoted by infinity.
